newsitem.title: USA: FedEx implements UPS strike contingencies.
newsitem.headline: FedEx implements UPS strike contingencies.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said Thursday it has seen "a dramatic increase in volume" as customers seek to avoid shipping disruptions that would arise from a strike at United Parcel Service of America Inc.

FedEx said it has implemented additional measures to maintain the reliability of the company's service while it and others in the shipping business await the outcome of the labor dispute between UPS and the International Brotherhood of Teamsters.
Unless UPS and the union reach an accord by midnight EDT, about two-thirds of UPS' domestic workforce of about 301,000 employees is set to strike, halting UPS operations.
FedEx said its first priority will be to maintain service levels for existing customers.
It will not, however, open new accounts until the UPS labor situation is resolved, it said.
The company said it has implemented the following steps:
-- Current FedEx customers will remain the company's first priority. The company is limiting current customers to their normal shipping volumes to maintain service.
-- FedEx will accept packages from customers who bring them to FedEx drop-off locations but the company will limit the quantity of packages it accepts.

-- Cut-off times at all drop-off locations are now two hours earlier than usual. FedEx will encourage customers to double-check the latest drop-off times where they normally leave their packages for any further changes.
-- As provided in its Service Guide and until further notice, FedEx will not offer money-back guarantees.
-- FedEx will continue to make regularly-scheduled stops, but will not schedule any new regular pick-up stops.
